evidence.finding: At a 390x844 viewport, the homepage Menu opened a labeled Mobile navigation containing About. Activating About reached https://staging-a.jamieburk.art/about with title About - Jamie Burkart. The path is one navigation action after opening the menu.

The About page visibly connects Open House, WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, NYC Artist Coalition, and source-backed team memory under Systems people can inhabit. It explicitly joins artistic, civic, technical, and social practice while keeping Jamie's technical-project-management and implementation role prominent.

The public through-line asks how structures help people recognize relationships, participate, remember, and continue. Its recursive sequence—observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document for continuation—distinguishes the practice from conventional administration.

More than three public-safe continuities are legible: WOWList turns organizer vocabulary into followable community infrastructure; Sunday Dinner / 196 turns hospitality, onboarding, and trust into repeatable participation systems; NYC Artist Coalition / FairRentNYC joins field meetings, public interfaces, source maps, and durable coalition memory; Harry J. Epstein connects customer and team relationships to maintained operational releases.

The FairRentNYC case study states that field work and technical work are one practice: conversations become shared public surfaces and paths others can continue. Visible examples include meetings, town halls, hearings, campaign sites, running minutes, question logs, action trackers, and source maps.

WOWList is consistently described as co-built and credits collaborators. FairRentNYC names many collaborators and expressly rejects sole causation for coalition and policy outcomes. Sunday Dinner identifies co-organizers where supported and credits the 196 / Sunday Dinner community.

Sunday Dinner / 196 publishes redacted workflow reconstructions while withholding participant names, contacts, attendance histories, correspondence, access details, proposals, photographs, and participant-level values. The source-backed-memory page keeps Known, Open, and Protected states distinct and rejects unsafe private-archive browsing.

No protected educational record, private correspondence, private archive path, participant-level record, unapproved testimonial, or romanticized vulnerability was observed on the reviewed public surfaces. Historical counts are bounded as snapshots rather than current activity, and research/method work is not presented as production deployment.
